question: An 18-year-old man presents with a sudden loss of consciousness while playing college football. There was no history of a concussion. Echocardiography shows left ventricular hypertrophy and increased thickness of the interventricular septum. Which is the most likely pathology underlying the present condition?

options.opb: Mutation in the myosin heavy chain

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy -> Left ventricular hypertrophy and interventricular septum thickening -> Sudden loss of consciousness -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely pathology underlying the present condition of an 18-year-old man with sudden loss of consciousness, left ventricular hypertrophy, and increased thickness of the interventricular septum is a mutation in the myosin heavy chain, specifically related to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
analysis: The most likely pathology underlying the sudden loss of consciousness in an 18-year-old man with left ventricular hypertrophy and increased thickness of the interventricular septum is hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, specifically related to a mutation in the myosin heavy chain. This condition is a common cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes.
